invariant_user_goal: Derive reusable operations from excellent designer lettering, validate on unseen different characters and multi-character compositions; glyph reconstruction alone is not success

source.source_license: CC BY 3.0; attribution and modification note required
source.caveat: These are static vector contour horizontal ink-run widths, not independent pen strokes, pressure, speed, real material behavior or designer process.

inputs.glyph_source: chanind/hanzi-writer-data / Make Me a Hanzi / Arphic Public License
inputs.topology: all conditions share target source medians

methods.A: uniform 26/1024 ink stroke applied to smooth centrelines
methods.C: reference-contour-width-quantiles conditioned hero/support/detail stroke tiers and tapered ends
methods.D: C with deterministic small-amplitude local width undulation
methods.common_input: same glyph content and same skeleton
methods.local_implementation: Python code and output images created in current workspace; downloadable ZIP delivered in conversation, not archived as GitHub bytes

actual_outputs.result: C qualitatively resembles smooth geometric vector calligraphy with narrower tails; ink character weight weaker than source and no proven professional aesthetic gain. D slight noise lacks meaningful visible uplift.

concurrent_result_awareness.relationship: The per-stroke BCSS annotation experiment is a stronger source route. This independent static-contour experiment confirms the no-gain finding but must not replace or supersede it.

newly_verified_external_constraints.DCOH120K: Provides x/y, stroke index, timestamp, tilt, pressure; repository says research access only after academic application and approval; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, cannot download/test or use commercially without permission
newly_verified_external_constraints.other_sources: HCSU provides rich annotated author/script/ink/stroke features under noncommercial CC BY-NC, but it is not time-series brush action and cannot prove creator steps

go_no_go.first_gate: Need 3+ same-artist licensed works with variable glyph topologies or genuine role-labelled stroke motion from same creative direction; measure role-specific brush/ink interactions and test against untouched held-out glyphs.
